property: Operational host protocol and principal-service base on the ARPANET was migrated from NCP to IP/TCP and TCP-based services through a staged transition ending with NCP removal from service.

date_or_range.notes: RFC 801 defines a staged migration, dual-protocol period and Full Internet Service milestone in January 1983.

sources.locator: General Plan; Milestones; Full Internet Service Jan 83
sources.supports: planned and operational removal of NCP in favor of IP/TCP environment

sources.locator: NCP to TCP mail transition strategy
sources.supports: service-level transition planning predating final cutover
sources.notes: Shows that the transition was a multi-service migration rather than one atomic protocol change.

negative_claims: This edge does not mean every host changed protocols simultaneously on one instant.
This edge does not mean Telnet, FTP and mail disappeared; their service roles continued with changed protocol foundations.
This edge does not reduce the transition to TCP alone; IP and application protocols/services were also involved.
open_questions: Build a host-by-host conversion timeline from NIC transition workbooks and site records.
Identify relay hosts and document actual NCP/TCP interworking traffic during 1981-1982.
Recover operator and user reports of transition failures/performance problems.
notes: Reference example of an operational replacement lineage with a documented coexistence/migration interval.
